citations.text: J. D. Porter (2019). Large, medium, and small problem instance data for experimental design and model validation in supply chain design. Mendeley Data, version 2 (data created by D. Nippaya).

description: Three-echelon supply chain design instances (plants, distribution centres, customers) in small, medium and large sizes, with low and high variants of each for a factorial experiment: plant and distribution centre capacities and fixed costs, customer demands, transit times and unit shipping costs from plants and from distribution centres to customers. graph/v1 is the target, as for other facility location data: plants, distribution centres and customers as typed nodes with capacity, fixed cost and demand, and the shipping lanes as edges with cost and transit time.
name: Supply chain design problem instances (Nippaya and Porter)

recipe.reason: Each instance is spread over up to six headerless tab-separated matrices (capacity and fixed cost per plant and per distribution centre, demand per customer, and customer by facility matrices of transit time and unit shipping cost), with a bare carriage return ending the demand file's lines and a different width for every file; the csv-table parser reads each file but names one set of columns per recipe, and turning the matrices into one graph needs a parser that joins the files of an instance, which keepset does not have.
